sources.title: New York skyline from Governors Island — Acacia Card Company postcard
sources.creator: Acacia Card Company (publisher); Tichnor Brothers (printer)
sources.researchNote: The Boston Public Library dates the card to about 1930–1945. The publisher’s imprint on the back, “258 Broadway, New York 7, N.Y.”, uses a postal zone number; the Post Office introduced zone numbers in 1943, so the card cannot be earlier. The view is later than Kaper’s arrival in 1935 and stands for the city, not for that day.

media.title: New York skyline from Governors Island — postcard, 1943–1945
media.description: Linen-finish picture postcard of the Lower Manhattan skyline seen across the harbour from Governors Island, published by the Acacia Card Company of New York as card 62289 and printed by Tichnor Brothers. The publisher’s address on the back includes the postal zone “New York 7”, so the card was printed in or after 1943, when postal zones were introduced.
media.altText: Coloured postcard of the skyscrapers of Lower Manhattan across blue water, framed by a tree and a hedge in the foreground.
media.publicCaption: The Lower Manhattan skyline from Governors Island, on a postcard printed between 1943 and 1945.
media.publicCreditLine: Acacia Card Company, New York, card 62289, printed by Tichnor Brothers; Boston Public Library, Tichnor Brothers Postcard Collection; via Digital Commonwealth.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The Acacia Card Company published the card in the United States between 1943 and 1945, and neither side carries a copyright notice; a work published in the United States before 1978 without notice entered the public domain on publication. The Boston Public Library, which holds the card, records no known copyright restrictions.

timelineEvents.title: Arrival in New York en route to Los Angeles
timelineEvents.label: 24 Oct 1934 · Arrival in New York
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper arrived in New York from France with Eleonora on a temporary visa, travelling onward to Los Angeles.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Kaper and his wife Eleonora sailed from Le Havre on 17 October 1934 aboard the S.S. Champlain in second cabin class and reached New York on 24 October. Their non-immigrant visas had been issued in Paris on 15 October, numbered in a single series with the Jurmanns’ (NI 1581–1584), and the manifest records Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer as having paid the passage and as the party they were joining in Culver City. Kaper gave his occupation as musician and declared that he meant to stay about eight months and then return, without seeking United States citizenship. David Blum of the Culver Export Corporation met them in New York, and they left for Hollywood on 27 October.

timelineEvents.title: Duke Ellington records “All God’s Chillun Got Rhythm”
timelineEvents.label: 8 Jun 1937 · Ellington records “All God’s Chillun Got Rhythm”
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Duke Ellington and His Famous Orchestra recorded “All God’s Chillun Got Rhythm” in New York, bringing a Kaper–Jurmann film song into the jazz repertoire.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Duke Ellington and His Famous Orchestra recorded “All God’s Chillun Got Rhythm” in New York on 8 June 1937 for Master (MA 137, matrix M 519-1). Written by Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann with words by Gus Kahn for A Day at the Races, the song passed from the screen into the jazz repertoire.

places.publicNote: Kaper and Eleonora arrived in New York after crossing the Atlantic from Le Havre aboard the S.S. Champlain, before travelling on to Los Angeles.
